nodes.n: 9 AM. Nets. Rain has stopped, mostly. Captain Sameer stands behind the net with a coffee and the expression of a man who has already decided something.

nodes.t: Harpreet. Bowl at him properly. If he's cover, I want to know what I'm covering with.

moment.title: Net Two
moment.desc: Harpreet Gill, 147 clicks. Fourteen players pretending not to watch. The captain is timing your feet. Survive four balls.

nodes.t: Hm. Nine times, they dropped that. Interesting.
Harpreet does that to everyone on day one. He did it to me. Again tomorrow.

nodes.n: Breakfast. Aryan sits alone at the window, walking a little too carefully to the toaster. Nobody notices. Except you.

nodes.th: Thursday is tomorrow. If I say nothing, he plays on a torn leg, and I fly home. If I say something, I play, and every newspaper in Delhi calls me a snake.

choice.d: It's his leg, but it's the team's World Cup.

choice.t: Sit down opposite Aryan. "Tell them yourself. Today."

nodes.n: You eat your eggs. Aryan catches your eye once and gives the smallest nod. It doesn't feel like a win.
The doctor listens, nods, and goes very pale. By lunch the whole hotel knows. By tea, so does Aryan.

nodes.t: You couldn't wait two days? Three years you've been waiting. You couldn't wait two days?

nodes.th: I don't answer. I don't need to.

nodes.n: He looks at his plate for a long time. Then he gets up, slowly, and walks to the doctor's table himself.

nodes.t: Don't think this makes us friends.

nodes.n: Afternoon. Media hour. Every new face gets fifteen minutes in front of the cameras. You get five, and four of them are about Aryan.
When the room clears, one reporter stays. Diya, with a brown envelope.

nodes.t: Selection meeting minutes. Three years. A friend in the Board office owes me a very big favour.
Every time, three selectors voted for you. Every time, the chairman used his veto. Nine vetoes. One name.

nodes.th: Bhandari. Not bad luck. Not "next time". One man, nine times.

nodes.t: If you go on record, this is front page tomorrow. If you don't, I still have a story. But it's weaker.

choice.t: "Not now. I want to win my place, not a headline."
"Forget the story. Chai? It's raining. That's practically Kerala."
choice.d: Take her out of this room.

nodes.t: Your bat first. Fine. But I'm keeping the envelope warm.
Are you sure? Once it's out, he'll know exactly who to blame.

nodes.n: The only chai in this town is a vending machine near the lifts. You buy two. They taste like warm cardboard. Diya drinks hers like it's from a roadside tea stall back home.

nodes.t: This is the worst chai I've ever had.
Ask me again tomorrow. Same machine.

nodes.n: She leaves the envelope on the table between you, and doesn't pick it up again.
Thursday. The fitness test. Ten sprints between cones, while a doctor holds a stopwatch and Prakash Bhandari holds his breath.
Aryan doesn't run. He sits on the bench with his leg strapped and his World Cup over. The announcement takes eleven words.

nodes.t: Warm-up game, Saturday. Number four. Fail, and you're on the first flight to Kochi. I'll drive you to the airport myself.

nodes.n: Aryan runs ten sprints. His face is grey by the sixth. He passes. Bhandari claps him on the back like a man who has won a horse race.

nodes.t: Both of you play Saturday. Aryan at five. You at four. I want to see something.
Fine. One game. Fail, and the cover goes home. Tidily.

nodes.cliff: Saturday. Number four. Fail, and they drop you a tenth time, in front of the world.
